Test: Non-invasive stability margin from output impedance
Purpose / failure mechanism: Sealed PMICs, LDOs and multi-loop converters expose no injection point, so PS-021 cannot be executed at all; a marginal loop still passes a single load step. Output-impedance peaking yields phase margin without breaking the loop, and the minor-loop-gain basis makes the same measurement applicable to input-filter interaction
Typical stimulus / conditions: Small-signal current modulation at the output, swept approximately 100 Hz–10 MHz, at Vin min/nom/max × load min/nom/max × Tmin/RT/Tmax, with minimum and maximum effective output capacitance
Measure / record: Zout(f) magnitude and phase, resonant peak frequency and Q, derived phase margin
Acceptance / target: Derived phase margin meets the design rule at every corner; no Zout resonance violating the rail noise/transient budget. The method saturates near 65–70°, so report ">70°" above that rather than a number
Equipment required: Keysight N6700 with N6775A and N6791A; thermal chamber; VNA/FRA with non-invasive stability capability; current injector; low-inductance 1:1 probing
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 sets the operating point. N6791A dynamic mode is not a calibrated small-signal injector; a VNA/FRA plus current injector is required
Main reference: OMICRON Lab Bode 100 output-impedance and non-invasive-stability application notes; Picotest NISM documentation; complements PS-021 and PS-023

Test: Effective capacitance under DC bias, temperature and ageing
Purpose / failure mechanism: Class-II MLCC loses a large fraction of rated capacitance under DC bias and at temperature extremes. The derated value moves the PS-021 crossover, the PS-007 ripple and the PS-008 transient envelope, yet is rarely re-measured after a BOM or supplier change
Typical stimulus / conditions: Measure input and output capacitor effective capacitance in-circuit or on coupons at 0 V and at the actual applied DC bias, across Tmin/RT/Tmax; repeat after endurance stress
Measure / record: Effective C vs DC bias and temperature; ESR over frequency; deviation from datasheet nominal; post-stress drift
Acceptance / target: Effective capacitance at worst-case bias and temperature stays inside the range assumed by the loop-compensation and ripple analyses
Equipment required: LCR meter or VNA with DC-bias capability; impedance adapters; thermal chamber
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can supply the DC bias in some fixtures but cannot measure capacitance; an LCR meter or impedance-capable VNA is required
Main reference: Capacitor manufacturer bias/temperature characteristics; AEC-Q200 Rev E; feeds PS-007, PS-008 and PS-021

Test: Audible noise from capacitors and magnetics
Purpose / failure mechanism: Class-II MLCC piezoelectric singing and magnetics noise are common late-stage NVH rejections. They appear specifically in the pulse-skipping, burst and light-load modes that PS-025 maps, and only in the final mechanical assembly
Typical stimulus / conditions: Sweep Vin × load × temperature including the light-load and dropout modes identified in PS-025; measure in a quiet enclosure at a defined distance, with the final mechanical assembly and mounting
Measure / record: Sound pressure level vs frequency; correlation with switching-mode transitions; tonality
Acceptance / target: Within the project NVH requirement across all operating modes; no tonal component in any mode reachable during normal vehicle operation
Equipment required: Measurement microphone and analyser; anechoic or low-noise enclosure; final mechanical assembly
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 sweeps the operating point; acoustic measurement needs its own instrumentation and a quiet environment. Chamber and load cooling fans preclude in-chamber measurement
Main reference: Project NVH requirement; capacitor manufacturer application notes; correlates with PS-025

Test: HV shielded-line conducted transients (injection and measurement)
Purpose / failure mechanism: Equipment on isolated supplies above 60 V DC sees a transient environment that TR-001…TR-004 do not cover. Applies only to HV-connected converters
Typical stimulus / conditions: Standardised pulses injected on shielded HV supply lines through the specified HV artificial network; also measure transients generated by the DUT
Measure / record: Functional status, clamp voltage and current, DUT-generated transient amplitude and duration
Acceptance / target: Functional performance status per test plan; emitted transients within the vehicle-manufacturer limit
Equipment required: HV transient generator and HV artificial network per the technical specification; HV-rated probing; safety enclosure and interlocks
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 cannot supply or bias an HV DC link. Entirely external; normally a laboratory service
Main reference: ISO/TS 7637-4:2020 (confirmed 2024); applies only where HV-001/HV-002 apply

Test: Transient generator verification
Purpose / failure mechanism: The matrix mandates measurement traceability for instruments but never verifies the transient generator itself. Two nominally compliant ISO 7637-2 generators can produce materially different pulses into the same load, so TR-001…TR-004 results are not comparable between laboratories without this step
Typical stimulus / conditions: Verify generator output waveform parameters into the specified verification load, before each campaign and after any service
Measure / record: Pulse amplitude, rise and fall time, duration, source impedance, repetition rate, burst structure; deviation from nominal
Acceptance / target: Generator parameters inside the tolerances of the verification method; verification date recorded with every TR-* result
Equipment required: Specified verification load and probing; wide-bandwidth oscilloscope and HV probe (oscilloscope already available)
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 has no role. The existing oscilloscope plus the specified verification load covers most of the work
Main reference: ISO 7637-5:2016; supports TR-001…TR-004 and TR-006

Test: Conducted immunity, extended audio range (15 Hz – 250 kHz)
Purpose / failure mechanism: Per-lead narrowband conducted immunity on power and output leads. Overlaps AUTO-006 in frequency but is a different test with a different coupling arrangement, per-lead application and its own severity levels. A converter can pass one and fail the other
Typical stimulus / conditions: Narrowband voltage injected per lead through the specified isolation-transformer coupling, 15 Hz–250 kHz, at the customer-named severity level
Measure / record: Functional status, output-voltage disturbance, false resets, current-sense and protection false trips
Acceptance / target: Required functional status across the whole sweep on every applicable lead
Equipment required: Audio oscillator and power amplifier (source impedance ≤2 Ω, 50 W into 0,5 Ω); coupling isolation transformer rated for the DC lead current; voltage and current measurement
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads the DUT; injection needs the specified oscillator, amplifier and coupling transformer. The N6791A may need isolating from the injection point
Main reference: ISO 11452-10:2009 (confirmed 2020); the relationship to AUTO-006 is to be recorded explicitly, not assumed

Test: Electrical fast transient/burst and surge on charging and mains-coupled lines
Purpose / failure mechanism: Required for type approval of charging-coupled products. Neither test exists anywhere in ISO 7637 or CISPR 25, so a plan built only from ISO references omits them entirely
Typical stimulus / conditions: EFT/burst at approximately ±2 kV open circuit, 5 ns/50 ns, 5 kHz repetition, at least one minute; surge 1,2/50 µs at ±2 kV line-to-earth and ±1 kV line-to-line on AC lines and ±0,5 kV on DC lines, five applications at 0°, 90°, 180° and 270°
Measure / record: Functional status, resets, communication errors, damage, protection-component stress
Acceptance / target: Per the regulation and the customer test plan; exact levels from the applicable revision
Equipment required: EFT/burst generator; combination-wave surge generator; coupling and decoupling networks
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can power the DUT if adequately decoupled, but must be protected from the injected transient. Generators and CDNs are external
Main reference: UN Regulation No. 10 Rev 7 Annexes 15 and 16 (in force 2025-06-17); applies only to charging-coupled or mains-coupled products

Test: Reverberation-chamber radiated immunity
Purpose / failure mechanism: Recognised by UN R10 Rev 7 as an alternative to the ALSE method of EMC-004. Often faster and cheaper for large harnesses, but the field statistics differ, so results are not numerically interchangeable with ALSE
Typical stimulus / conditions: Expose DUT and harness in a mode-stirred reverberation chamber over the specified frequency range and severity
Measure / record: Functional status, output voltage, communications, faults; chamber calibration data
Acceptance / target: Required functional status; record which method was used, because ALSE and reverberation results are not directly comparable
Equipment required: Reverberation chamber with mode stirrer; RF generation and amplification; field probes
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads only
Main reference: ISO 11452-11, recognised by UN R10 Rev 7; alternative to EMC-004

Test: Sub-200 MHz alternative immunity methods (TEM cell, stripline, DPI)
Purpose / failure mechanism: Below roughly 200 MHz, ALSE antennas become large and inefficient and ISO 11452-2 itself points to other parts. Direct RF power injection in particular is the practical route to an IC-level immunity margin during design iteration rather than at qualification
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply the selected method per its part of ISO 11452 at the customer-named severity level
Measure / record: Functional status; for DPI, forward power at failure per pin
Acceptance / target: Required functional status; for design iteration, record the margin rather than only pass/fail
Equipment required: TEM cell, stripline fixture, or DPI coupling network with RF generator, amplifier and directional coupler
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads only; the coupling fixture and RF chain are external
Main reference: ISO 11452-3 (TEM cell), ISO 11452-5 (stripline), ISO 11452-7 (DPI); ISO 11452-2 points below 200 MHz to parts 4, 3 and 5

Test: Insulation coordination and partial-discharge verification
Purpose / failure mechanism: AUTO-019 and AUTO-020 are one-shot pass/fail tests. For a barrier switching at tens of kilohertz with fast edges, the wear-out mechanism is partial discharge in voids inside the insulation system, which a dielectric-withstand test passes without detecting
Typical stimulus / conditions: Derive required clearance, creepage and impulse withstand from working voltage, overvoltage category and pollution degree; then measure partial-discharge inception and extinction voltage across the barrier, before and after humidity and temperature-cycling stress
Measure / record: Measured clearance and creepage; impulse-withstand result; PD inception and extinction voltage; drift after stress
Acceptance / target: Coordination satisfied with margin; PD extinction voltage above the maximum working voltage across the barrier, including after environmental stress
Equipment required: Partial-discharge test set; impulse generator; mechanical clearance measurement; safety enclosure
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 has no role. Specialised HV insulation equipment and a safety enclosure are required
Main reference: IEC 60664-1; IEC 62477-1; SAE 2013-01-1528; extends AUTO-019 and AUTO-020

Test: Common-mode transient immunity across the isolation barrier
Purpose / failure mechanism: An isolated converter's feedback, gate-drive and communication paths cross the barrier and see the full common-mode dV/dt of the HV switching node. Insufficient common-mode transient immunity appears as data corruption, false shutdown or duty-cycle disturbance rather than as a barrier failure, so HV-003 will not find it
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply defined common-mode dV/dt steps across the barrier at the worst-case rate the application produces; sweep operating point and temperature
Measure / record: Bit errors, feedback disturbance, false fault assertions, output disturbance during the transient
Acceptance / target: No functional upset at the maximum dV/dt the application can produce, with the margin required by the component datasheet
Equipment required: Common-mode transient generator or representative switching fixture; isolated high-bandwidth probing; differential probes
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads; the common-mode stimulus and isolated probing are external
Main reference: Isolator and gate-driver datasheet CMTI ratings; product requirement; complements HV-003

Test: Power-module power cycling (PCsec / PCmin)
Purpose / failure mechanism: Where a power stage uses a power module, bond-wire and solder fatigue are driven by junction-temperature swing, not ambient. TH-005 and LIFE-002 cycle the ambient and do not reproduce ΔTj. Results verify the manufacturer's lifetime model against the mission profile
Typical stimulus / conditions: PCsec and PCmin power cycling to the defined ΔTj with the end-of-life criteria defined for the module technology; extend with high/low-temperature storage and HTRB/HTGB/H3TRB as applicable. For SiC add dynamic gate stress, dynamic reverse bias and dynamic H3TRB
Measure / record: Cycles to first end-of-life criterion; Vce(on) or Rds(on) drift; thermal-resistance drift; bond and solder condition
Acceptance / target: Cycles to failure consistent with the mission profile and the manufacturer lifetime model, with the required margin
Equipment required: Power-cycling test system with junction-temperature determination; module-level fixturing
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 cannot perform module power cycling. Dedicated equipment is required; usually a laboratory service
Main reference: ECPE Guideline AQG 324 Rel. 04.1/2025 (based on LV 324); applies only to power-module-based stages

Test: Biased humidity (H3TRB / THB) and electrochemical migration
Purpose / failure mechanism: TH-007 and TH-010 apply humidity without electrical bias. Electrochemical migration and dendrite growth need moisture **plus** a potential gradient, so an unbiased humidity test can pass a board that fails in service
Typical stimulus / conditions: Apply the specified temperature and humidity with the DUT electrically biased for the required duration; include high-impedance feedback and sense nodes in the biased set
Measure / record: Leakage current over time; insulation resistance; parametric drift; post-test inspection for migration and corrosion
Acceptance / target: No migration or corrosion; leakage and parametric drift inside limits; post-test function per requirement
Equipment required: Temperature/humidity chamber with bias feed-throughs; leakage-current monitoring. The existing thermal chamber is insufficient unless humidity-capable
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 can supply the bias if the chamber has suitable feed-throughs and the campaign is long-running; leakage monitoring needs a low-current instrument
Main reference: ECPE AQG 324 H3TRB; AEC-Q101 and AEC-Q200 biased-humidity tests; extends TH-007 and TH-010

Test: Low air pressure / altitude
Purpose / failure mechanism: Altitude reduces convective cooling and simultaneously reduces the withstand of clearances, so both derate together. A design verified at sea level can fail thermally and electrically at altitude. Neither TH-001 nor AUTO-020 covers it
Typical stimulus / conditions: Operate at full load at the specified reduced pressure and elevated temperature; repeat dielectric withstand at reduced pressure where the barrier relies on clearance rather than solid insulation
Measure / record: Case and component temperatures against the sea-level baseline; thermal-derating shift; breakdown or flashover at reduced pressure
Acceptance / target: Meets thermal derating and dielectric requirements at the specified maximum operating altitude
Equipment required: Altitude/low-pressure chamber, ideally combined with temperature; dielectric-withstand capability inside the chamber for the electrical part
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6700 supplies and loads if feed-throughs exist; the pressure chamber is external
Main reference: IEC 60068-2-13; IEC 60664-1 altitude correction; confirm whether the customer specification or the ISO 16750-4 edition in force imposes a level

Test: Protection coordination and selectivity with the vehicle-side fuse
Purpose / failure mechanism: PS-014 and PS-015 characterise the converter's own limits in isolation. They do not establish whether the converter protects before or after the upstream vehicle fuse. Miscoordination means a field fault opens a fuse the service network cannot reset, instead of triggering a recoverable converter shutdown
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject the fault set of PS-015, PS-030 and PS-018 through the representative harness and the actual vehicle-side fuse; repeat at temperature corners
Measure / record: Fault current against time; I²t delivered to the fuse; converter protection trip time; whether the fuse opened; final recoverable state
Acceptance / target: Coordination matches the intended strategy at every fault type and temperature corner; no unintended fuse operation for faults the converter is supposed to clear
Equipment required: Representative fuse and harness; wide-bandwidth current measurement; the existing oscilloscope; sacrificial fuses
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A powers the input through the fuse under test while N6791A and the short-circuit fixture create the fault. Within module ratings this is largely executable on the present bench
Main reference: ISO 8820 fuse series; vehicle-manufacturer harness protection concept; extends PS-014, PS-015, PS-018 and PS-030

Test: Non-volatile memory and reflash integrity during supply interruption
Purpose / failure mechanism: AUTO-009 records NVM status but nothing deliberately interrupts the supply during a flash write or an over-the-air reflash. A write interrupted mid-sector can corrupt calibration, configuration or safety parameters in a way that survives the next power cycle and never appears as an electrical failure
Typical stimulus / conditions: Inject interruptions of the AUTO-010 duration set at randomised phases during NVM writes and during a full reflash; repeat across the brownout band mapped by AUTO-009; high repetition count
Measure / record: Post-interruption NVM integrity; checksum/CRC status; bootloader recovery path; diagnostic trouble codes; whether the unit remains field-recoverable
Acceptance / target: No undetected corruption. Every interruption ends in a defined state: valid image, or detected-invalid with a working recovery path
Equipment required: Fast MOSFET interruption fixture with randomised phase control; DUT diagnostic interface; automation for high repetition counts
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A supplies; the deterministic fast fault-injection controller described in the bench automation document is required for sub-millisecond phase control. Stream to the control computer for long campaigns
Main reference: Product requirement; internal safety analysis; extends AUTO-009 and AUTO-010

Test: Quiescent current with bus activity and partial-network wake
Purpose / failure mechanism: AUTO-015 measures sleep current in a quiet state. Real key-off current is dominated by periodic bus wake events and partial-networking frames, so a unit that meets the static budget can still exceed the daily energy budget
Typical stimulus / conditions: Measure over a representative key-off period with realistic bus traffic and partial-networking wake patterns, across voltage and temperature; integrate energy rather than sampling current
Measure / record: Current profile over time; wake-event count and duration; integrated charge and energy per day
Acceptance / target: Vehicle-manufacturer daily energy budget met with realistic bus activity, not only static sleep current
Equipment required: Bus interface and traffic generator; high-dynamic-range current measurement with wide bandwidth and long record; control computer
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6775A supplies, but its 3 mA current resolution cannot resolve microamp sleep floors or fast wake spikes. A dynamic-range-capable instrument is required, as for AUTO-015
Main reference: LV 124 E-19; vehicle-manufacturer closed-circuit current budget; extends AUTO-015 and PS-006

Test: Power-flow direction change and mode transition
Purpose / failure mechanism: 48V-001 and FUSA-011 assume unidirectional flow. In a bidirectional 48 V↔12 V unit the transition itself is the hazard: dead-time errors, control-mode handover and reverse-recovery stress occur only during direction change and are invisible to every steady-state test
Typical stimulus / conditions: Command direction changes at every combination of source voltage, load and temperature, including commanded reversal during a load transient and during a supply disturbance; include repeated fast reversals
Measure / record: Transition time; excursion on both rails during handover; shoot-through or cross-conduction current; switch voltage stress during reversal; mode-flag consistency
Acceptance / target: No rail excursion outside requirement on either side; no cross-conduction; deterministic transition timing at every corner
Equipment required: Second source on the opposite side; bidirectional or four-quadrant capability; the existing oscilloscope; high-bandwidth current probing
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: N6791A sinks but cannot source, so it cannot emulate the opposite-side battery. A second source or four-quadrant instrument is required
Main reference: Product requirement; ISO 21780:2020 functional-status framework; applies only to bidirectional converters

Test: Dual-source arbitration and inter-net fault propagation
Purpose / failure mechanism: With both nets energised the unit must decide which side sources, and must not let a fault on one net propagate to the other. Extends AUTO-018 to the case where both sides are independently powered and either can fail
Typical stimulus / conditions: Energise both nets at independent voltages including out-of-range and 0 V; inject the fault set of PS-030 and FUSA-011 on each side in turn; include loss of one net during power transfer
Measure / record: Current between nets; unintended powering; voltage excursion on the healthy net during a fault on the faulted net; isolation action and timing
Acceptance / target: Within the allowed inter-net current; a fault on one net never drives the other outside its requirement
Equipment required: Two independent sources; ammeters on both sides; fault-injection fixture
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: Requires a second independent source in addition to the N6775A, plus current measurement on both nets
Main reference: Extends AUTO-018 and FUSA-011; ISO 21780:2020; internal safety analysis

Test: Mission-profile-based robustness validation and margin mapping
Purpose / failure mechanism: LIFE-005 is the only row that measures margin rather than compliance. Without a mission profile the durations in LIFE-001 and LIFE-004 and the cycle counts in TH-005 have no derivation, and a pass says nothing about how much margin exists
Typical stimulus / conditions: Build the mission profile (temperature collective, voltage collective, cycles, operating hours, humidity, vibration over life); derive the knowledge matrix of dominant failure mechanisms; stress representative samples to failure on each; map the distance between specification limit, first functional failure and destructive failure
Measure / record: Mission profile document; failure-mechanism matrix; measured margin per mechanism; identification of the limiting mechanism
Acceptance / target: Every dominant mechanism has quantified margin against the mission profile. A test-to-pass result with no margin figure does not close this row
Equipment required: The present bench covers the electrical and thermal mechanisms; mechanical, humidity and component mechanisms need the corresponding facilities
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: The N6700 bench plus chamber already supports step-stress on the electrical and thermal mechanisms. This row is mainly planning and analysis work that redirects existing tests
Main reference: SAE J1211:2012 / ZVEI Robustness Validation Handbook; SAE J1879 for semiconductors; frames LIFE-005 and the combined-corner campaign

Test: Component qualification grade against mission profile
Purpose / failure mechanism: PS-029 verifies derating against datasheet limits but nothing checks that the parts are qualified for the location. A Grade 1 IC in a Grade 0 location, or an industrial-grade MLCC substituted for an automotive-grade part with the same value and case size, passes every bench test in this matrix and fails in the field
Typical stimulus / conditions: Review the bill of materials against the AEC qualification evidence: grade against the mission-profile temperature; qualification family against the actual part number and dielectric; whether short-circuit reliability data exists for smart power devices in the protection path
Measure / record: Per-part grade, qualification family and evidence reference; exceptions list with rationale; gaps against the mission profile
Acceptance / target: Every part qualified to a grade covering its mission-profile conditions, or a documented and accepted exception
Equipment required: Document review; no bench equipment
N6700 mapping with N6775A + N6791A: No bench role. A documentation verification that feeds PS-029, LIFE-004 and the FMEDA behind FUSA-006
Main reference: AEC-Q100 Rev J; AEC-Q101 and AEC-Q101-006; AEC-Q200 Rev E; AEC-Q104; feeds PS-029 and FUSA-006
